title: 第23章 骑士的启程第24章 出发时刻的阻碍
slug: 骑士先生魔王真的不存在啊
lines: 第23章骑士的启程
新约镇是个小地方，但大多数东西还是能够自给自足的。
在东边有一个牲畜市场，沿途走来可以看到鸡鸭鹅被关在笼子里，还有猎户会将猎物带到这里贩卖。
姆莉跟着唐一路来此，听着两侧的吆喝，感觉比她这些天在镇上各处都要热闹，也就仅次于酒馆。
辛西这一路也在好奇地左顾右盼，他是第一次来这种地方，对这里的一切都很好奇。
“嘿！兔崽子，小哥，要不要小兔崽子？便宜卖！”一位猎户坐在地上吆喝着，看见了辛西在注视他的货，便主动向他招手。
辛西立即走到猎户这边往笼子里看了几眼，这猎户也是热情，看辛西有兴趣，就主动打开笼子抓了一只卖相好的摆出来给他看。
“小兔崽子便宜，三十铜币一只。”猎户龇牙笑道。
辛西看这兔子可爱，有些心动，可他摸摸口袋，却是笑着摇头拒绝了。
“抱歉，我带不走它，没地方养。”辛西找了个借口就起身准备离开。
猎户看他要走，又拦住了他：“养不了可以杀了吃呀，虽然小了点，但味道也很不错，做一顿夜宵下酒美得很！”
辛西闻言愣住，看看可爱的兔子，怎么都想不到兔肉餐的模样。于是连忙摇头，很快跑回了唐的身边。
唐听着动静往后看了一眼，又深深看了眼猎户抓回笼中的兔子，什么都没问，只是默默将这件事记在了心里。
“唐，你理想中的坐骑是什么样的？”看着四周的家禽和小猎物，姆莉顺口就问了唐这个问题，她真的很难想象在这种地方能找到什么像样的坐骑。
“巨龙。”唐毫不犹豫地回答道。
“我是说，在这个地方。”
“独角兽。”
姆莉有些无语，这个地方能买到独角兽？虽然断了角的独角兽有可能被当成普通马匹，然后被送到这里贩卖，但这种概率真的很低。
就在这时，一道声音叫住了唐。
“嘿！唐，来大娘这里！”向唐招手说话的是一位高龄妇女，面相和蔼，身后还有好几笼子的小鸡。
“什么事？大娘？”唐好奇地走了过去。
他这口中的“大娘”并无亲缘关系，只是新约镇方言里一种类似于“大婶”、“阿姨”的称呼。
“你之前救了我女儿回来，听说今天还帮骑士团把之前镇上失踪的人也带回来了，一直没什么机会去你家拜访，这不是看你来买牲畜了吗？”
说话间，大娘转身提起了一小笼的鸡崽递给了唐。
“这小鸡崽子你收去，就当大娘感谢你救我女儿，也救了大家的一份心意。”
唐立即抬手挡住：“大娘，那都是身为一名骑士该做的，我今天是来买坐骑的，鸡崽带回去也没处养，便谢过您的心意了。”
大娘一听，露出了震惊的表情：“呀！你册封骑士了呀？！唐，有出息了！”
唐乐呵笑了两声，没做回答。
“不过啊，唐，你也知道我们镇上没骡子没马，甚至连一头驴都找不到。”大娘开始替唐为难起来了。
“我想找找，有牛也好。”唐说。
“没牛，镇上就没有什么牛。”大娘摇头，转头给唐指了个方向，“你往这里进去，兴许可以看到一些鹿啊、羊啊之类的。”
唐点头，谢过大娘的指示，又带着辛西与姆莉深入牲畜市场。
别说，还真让唐在某位猎户那看见了一只高大的麋鹿被关在笼子里。
content_en:
Chapter 23 The Knight’s Departure
New Testament Town is a small place, but it is self-sufficient in most things.
There is a livestock market on the east side. Along the way, you can see chickens, ducks and geese kept in cages, and hunters will bring their prey here to sell.
Mu Li followed Tang all the way here. Listening to the shouts on both sides, she felt that it was busier than anywhere else in the town she had been in these days, second only to the tavern.
Xinxi was also looking around curiously along the way. This was his first time in a place like this and he was very curious about everything here.
"Hey! You bastard, brother, do you want a little bastard? It's cheap!" A hunter was sitting on the ground and shouted. He saw Xinxi looking at his goods and waved to him.
Xinxi immediately walked over to the hunter and took a few glances into the cage. The hunter was also enthusiastic. Seeing that Xinxi was interested, he took the initiative to open the cage and catch a good-looking one and put it out for him to see.
"Little bastards are cheap, thirty copper coins each." Orion bared his teeth and smiled.
Xinxi saw how cute the rabbit was and was a little moved, but when he touched his pocket, he smiled and shook his head in rejection.
"Sorry, I can't take it with me, there's no place to keep it." Xinxi made an excuse and stood up to leave.
Seeing that he was about to leave, Orion stopped him again: "If you can't keep it, you can kill it and eat it. Although it is a little small, it tastes very good. It will be delicious as a late night snack with wine."
Xinxi was stunned when she heard this. Looking at the cute rabbit, she couldn't imagine what a rabbit meat meal would look like. So he shook his head quickly and quickly ran back to Tang's side.
Tang glanced back after listening to the movement, and then took a deep look at the rabbit that the hunter had captured in the cage. He didn't ask anything, but silently kept the matter in his heart.
"Tang, what is your ideal mount like?" Looking at the poultry and small prey around, Muli asked Tang this question casually. It was really hard for her to imagine that she could find any decent mount in a place like this.
"The dragon." Tang replied without hesitation.
"I mean, in this place."
"Unicorn."
Mli was speechless. Can you buy unicorns in this place? Although it is possible that unicorns with broken horns were treated as ordinary horses and then sent here for sale, the probability of this is really low.
At this moment, a voice stopped Tang.
"Hey! Tang, come to Auntie!" The person who waved to Tang and spoke was an elderly woman with a kind face and several cages of chickens behind her.
"What's the matter? Auntie?" Tang walked over curiously.
The "aunt" in his mouth is not related to her, but is just a term similar to "aunt" or "aunt" in the dialect of New Testament Town.
"You rescued my daughter before, and I heard that today you helped the knights to bring back the missing people in the town. I haven't had a chance to visit your house. Isn't it because you came to buy livestock?"
As she spoke, the aunt turned around and picked up a small cage of chickens and handed them to Tang.
"Take this little chicken and treat it like a mother-in-law thanking you for saving my daughter and saving everyone's heart."
Tang immediately raised his hand to block it: "Mom, that's what a knight should do. I'm here to buy a mount today. I don't have any place to raise the chickens when I take them home, so I thank you for your kindness."
When the aunt heard this, she showed a shocked expression: "Ah! You have been canonized as a knight?! Tang, you are promising!"
Tang Lehe laughed twice but did not answer.
"But, Tang, you also know that there are no mules or horses in our town, and we can't even find a donkey." The aunt began to feel embarrassed for Tang.
"I want to look for it, if there is a cow," Tang said.
"If there are no cows, there won't be any cows in the town." The aunt shook her head and turned to point Tang in the direction, "If you go in here, you might be able to see some deer, sheep and the like."
Tang nodded, thanked his aunt for the instruction, and took Cinxi and Muli deep into the livestock market.
Not to mention, Tang actually saw a tall elk locked in a cage at a hunter's house.
